channel.title: Wire — Databases
channel.description: Databases from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: The reverts will continue until morale improves
item.description: Many readers will be aware that an unusually high number of features have been reverted from the PostgreSQL 19 branch after the beta period began. Having some reverts is not unusual, maybe one per cycle could be expected. (2 sources: lobsters, postgresweekly)

item.title: pg_vectorsearch: A Partition-Based Alternative to HNSW
item.description: pg_vectorsearch is a new open-source Postgres extension. Its PRISM index serves 100M vectors in 6 ms on 4x less RAM than HNSW, with builds in under 2 hours. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: Don't Bet on SELECT Order: Shuffle Your Rows and See What Folds
item.description: PostgreSQL does not guarantee row order without ORDER BY. Use Rails 8.2 or pg_disorder to shuffle unordered SELECT results and expose hidden order dependencies, flaky tests, and application bugs. (2 sources: postgresweekly, rubyweekly)

item.title: Agent Memory: Raw Retrieval Vs. Extracted Facts, Tested
How Savepoints Throttled Our Postgres Queue
item.description: Our on-call ticker runs on a Postgres-backed queue. Under load test it slowed to a crawl, and adding workers only made it worse. The culprit was a savepoint per tick, minting a MultiXact on every locked row. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: ran 800 hours of benchmarks on the Postgres 19 betas
item.description: Yay, “That time of the year”™ again soon 🎉 This time maybe with a bit more fuzz / excitement / anxiety as usual - due to various obstacles surrounding the release as detailed in a few recent posts by various people. (1 source: postgresweekly)
